findings.body: The function register_shipment_events uses events: list[str] = [] as a default parameter. In Python, default arguments are evaluated once at function definition time, so the same list object is shared across all calls. Subsequent calls will accumulate events from previous calls, causing data corruption. When register_shipment_events is called multiple times, the events list from previous calls persists, causing the function to return merged events from all calls instead of just the current call. For example, calling register_shipment_events('a') then register_shipment_events('b') returns {'b': ['a', 'b']} instead of {'b': ['b']}.
findings.failure_scenario: When register_shipment_events is called multiple times, the events list from previous calls persists, causing the function to return merged events from all calls instead of just the current call.
